purpose: Designing the complete layer stack for a gold-plated piece — which strike, barrier or underplate class, gold build class, and topcoat class go onto which substrate, in what order and why — so that adhesion, diffusion blocking, wear-class fit, nickel-release compliance, honest naming, and per-layer verifiability are engineered into the stack before a single ampere is delivered.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the piece arrives from the preparation chain clean, active, and water-break-free; prep-chain execution and bath health are owned by sibling specialists
every layer is deposited from a purchased commercial plating system operated inside its supplier technical data sheet; no DIY bath formulation from raw chemicals
published handbook-class ranges are cited only as handbook-class ranges; the specific product's TDS and the shop's own logged runs govern setpoints

regulatory thresholds — nickel release, regulated marketing terms, waste and discharge rules — are named as obligation classes and verified against current rules in the destination jurisdiction before release

cyanide-bearing and acid chemistries are segregated by the shop safety program: never mixed, never stored together, never sharing a drain; formal training governs hazardous procedure, never improvisation
exclusions: surface-area estimation, current-density selection, Faraday-based time-thickness estimation, rectifier setup and verification, and current-distribution tooling such as shielding and auxiliary anode classes — the Electrical Control & Thickness Delivery KB owns delivering the microns this KB specifies

rack versus barrel versus brush-selective decisions, wiring and contact-point placement, agitation and part positioning, drag-out management, inter-tank rinse sequencing, and run-logging mechanics — the Fixturing, Racking & Run Handling KB owns physical execution of the stack this KB designs

cleaning, pickling, electrocleaning, and activation-chain execution — the preparation specialist owns the pre-plate chain; this KB consumes its clean active output and specifies only which strike class the stack opens with and why
bath make-up, titration and analysis schedules, replenishment, and contamination treatment — the bath-chemistry specialist owns bath health; this KB names bath classes and their TDS references only

numeric bath setpoints, prices, and wear-life or thickness guarantees stated as fact — parameters appear as mechanisms or qualitative bands; the product TDS and the shop's logged history carry the numbers
mains-side electrical work of any kind — all equipment runs within its manufacturer's instructions, with no improvisation past the rectifier's own manual
personalized medical or legal advice on nickel allergy or chemical exposure — such questions route to regulation classes and professional care
forcing a piece that cannot be racked or contacted without damage — that situation escalates to an intake/customer decision, never to improvised force

competency_questions.question: Given this piece — its substrate, wear situation, destination market, and forming plan — what full layer stack goes on it, in what order, and what is each layer's job?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer names every layer as a class with a stated job and thickness class, sequenced strike then build then barrier then gold then topcoat, and traces each choice to a line in the intake brief

competency_questions.question: Why does thin gold plated straight over sterling silver or brass look tarnished within weeks, and what actually stops it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: silver or copper/zinc migration through thin gold is named as the mechanism, with an adequate barrier layer or a heavier gold build plus written disclosure named as the counters — never a bath adjustment

competency_questions.question: Which strike does this substrate need before any build layer, and under what conditions may a strike legitimately be skipped?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the strike class is matched to the substrate class (Wood's-class for passive metals, copper-strike class for steel/zinc with the non-cyanide type preferred, gold strike at the noble end), skips are documented decisions, and the displacement-deposit hazard is cited for every bare-metal-meets-noble-bath interface

competency_questions.question: Can nickel stay in the stack for this skin-contact piece, and what must happen before it does?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer treats nickel release as a finished-stack property governed by a regulation class (EN 1811-class testing under REACH-class restriction as the anchor example), requires a verified current-rules check for the destination jurisdiction, and defaults to nickel-free where no compliance basis exists

competency_questions.question: What are the nickel-free barrier options, and what does each cost in ductility, analysis burden, and price exposure?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: palladium-class thin-flash barriers (with the hydrogen-microcracking veto on thick builds) and white-bronze Cu-Sn-Zn class (hard, brittle, analysis-heavy, cyanide-type safety implications) are both named with their trade-offs, chosen by wear class and forming plan rather than preference

competency_questions.question: Flash or heavy gold build for this piece, and what wear expectation gets disclosed with it before sale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the build class follows the wear class, hang-only pieces may be honest flash with barrier or sealing, rub-and-knock classes need build or an explicitly disclosed short-life positioning, and the tint-through limit of flash over white barriers is acknowledged

competency_questions.question: When does a copper leveling layer belong in the stack, and what must never sit directly above it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: copper is justified by surface-quality economics (leveling, polishing base for heavy builds), always sits over a strike on steel or zinc, and is never the layer directly under thin gold — a barrier always intervenes

competency_questions.question: Why does a duplex or multi-layer system outlast one thick layer, and when is another layer NOT worth its tank?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the answer explains layered corrosion-path interruption and per-layer specialization, and refuses layers that have no named job because every added interface is an adhesion risk and a cost

competency_questions.question: Which topcoat class — molecular passivate, e-coat, sol-gel, lacquer class, or none — fits this piece, and what does each trade away?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: molecular films are offered where feel must survive and abrasion is low, film classes where wear demands armor, the aging/feel/cure bills of films are stated, hexavalent-chromate passivates are excluded outright, and every film waits until forming is complete

competency_questions.question: May this piece be sold as vermeil, gold plated, or gold filled — and who decides, the stack or the listing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: each term is treated as a regulated class verified against current destination-market rules, the term follows the verified stack and never the reverse, electroplated goods never carry gold-filled or rolled-gold names, and plated goods are never represented as solid gold

competency_questions.question: The piece will be sized or bent after plating — which stacks survive that, and which crack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: stack ductility is located in the underplate choice (sulfamate-class ductile, bright nickel and white bronze brittle), hard topcoats are deferred until after forming, and form-first-plate-after is offered as the re-sequencing escape

competency_questions.question: How is the finished stack proven right, layer by layer, before the piece is released?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the plan names adhesion coupons (bend/wrap or heat-quench, ASTM-B571-class), per-layer XRF thickness classes with microsection as referee class, porosity classes for sweat wear, and nickel-release testing classes wherever nickel remains in a skin-contact stack — written before the first tank

competency_questions.question: What must the run sheet contain so the electrical-delivery and fixturing KBs can execute this stack without asking its designer anything?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: layer order with jobs and thickness classes, a commercial product and TDS reference per bath, strike and live-entry flags at sensitive interfaces, attached compliance and term verdicts, verification hooks, and the disclosed wear expectation are all present and executable by a second operator

glossary.definition: A deliberately thin, adhesion-first deposit run at low cathodic efficiency whose only job is to make the next layer's bond — activating or covering a difficult surface at bath entry. A strike that grows into a build layer has failed its own definition.

A functional layer between substrate and gold that blocks substrate atoms from migrating into the thin gold, levels the surface, and carries corrosion duty a sub-micron gold coat cannot; nickel classes, palladium classes, white bronze, and copper-plus-barrier pairs are the working families.

The high-acid, low-efficiency nickel strike class that simultaneously strips the self-healing passive film of stainless or aged nickel and deposits fresh bonded nickel in the same instant — the canonical adhesion answer for passive metals, run per its commercial product's TDS.

A Cu-Sn-Zn alloy barrier class: bright white, tarnish-resistant, nickel-free, and hard but less ductile than nickel; alloy ratio drifts with operating conditions, making it an analysis-heavy bath best run as a proprietary system with supplier TDS and analysis support.

A two-layer nickel system class (semi-bright under bright) engineered so corrosion paths that penetrate one layer dead-end at the interface with the next — corrosion-path interruption by architecture rather than by sheer thickness.

A color-only class of gold coat, thin enough that it exists for appearance and pricing rather than wear; below a tint-through threshold class the color of the layer beneath reads through, and porosity rises as the flash thins.

The regulation-anchored test class (EN 1811-class measurement, EN 12472-class wear simulation) for how much nickel a finished worn article releases through its whole stack; a compliance property of the stack, not of any single bath, with limits verified in the current rules of the destination jurisdiction.

A regulated term class for gold-plated articles whose governing definitions typically require a silver substrate plus minimum gold thickness and karat conditions that vary by jurisdiction; the term is only usable when the verified stack meets the destination market's current definition.

Electrophoretic clear lacquer class: the rinsed part becomes an electrode in a waterborne polymer emulsion and a DC field deposits a self-limiting, recess-following film that is then oven-cured — the precision film topcoat behind long-lived fashion gold, including gold-tinted variants that are honest only with disclosed labeling.

The dark, spongy, zero-adhesion film formed when a less-noble metal enters a more-noble metal's solution without current — the substrate dissolves and the noble metal plates out uncontrolled; everything deposited over it peels, which is why strikes and live entry exist.

nodes.definition: Translate the job on the bench into stack-design inputs before any layer is chosen: what the substrate is claimed to be and what evidence backs the claim, how the piece will actually be worn, whether it touches skin, which market it ships to, whether it will be formed or sized after plating, what look the customer expects, and which regulated term the seller intends to use at listing. The brief also records heirloom and irreplaceability risk in writing, because a plated stack on an inherited piece is close to irreversible without a stripping cycle that carries its own hazard, and it captures the customer conversation that later disclosure rests on. Every downstream stack decision cites a line in this brief; a stack designed without one is a guess wearing a lab coat.

excluded: bath condition assessment (chemistry specialist)
racking feasibility judgment (fixturing KB)
price negotiation

pros.claim: A complete brief lets one stack template answer most jobs and makes later disputes resolvable from paper instead of memory
pros.example: a single line reading brass cuff, daily wear, EU customer forces the nickel-free question before any tank is touched

cons.claim: A full intake interview slows small jobs where the answer is obvious
cons.example: a steel keychain flash job does not need a forming-plan conversation, and insisting on one costs goodwill

failure_modes: accepting the customer's metal claim with no physical evidence
skipping the skin-contact question on items sold as decor but worn as jewelry
no written heirloom sign-off before plating an inherited piece
acceptance_tests: the brief record contains substrate evidence, wear class inputs, skin-contact answer, destination jurisdiction, forming plan, term intent, and the heirloom flag before stack design begins
revisit_triggers: a new destination market appears in the order flow
a return or dispute traces to a question the intake form never asked

base.update_signal: a logged dispute or warranty return that traces to a field the intake brief never captured

nodes.definition: Pin down what metal the stack must bond to and what that metal does to a stack: sterling and fine silver (fast migrators into thin gold), brass and jeweler's bronze (zinc-bearing, prone to dezincification and Zn/Cu migration), copper (migrates but plates easily), mild steel (rusts, needs full barrier duty), stainless (a self-healing passive film that reforms in seconds, putting it in strike territory), zinc die-cast (dissolves in acid baths, alkaline-first territory), and previously-plated or mystery white metal (treated as passive-prone until identified). Identification uses non-destructive evidence first — magnet, heft, hallmark reading, XRF where the shop has it — and escalates to the customer before any destructive spot test, because the test itself can be the damage on an heirloom.

included: escalation rule for unknowns and destructive tests
excluded: executing the cleaning or pickling chain (prep specialist)
assay-grade metallurgical analysis beyond bench evidence

pros.claim: Correct substrate identification makes half the stack design automatic
pros.example: reading a piece as 304-class stainless converts the plan to Wood's-strike-first without further debate

cons.claim: Bench-level identification has honest limits
cons.example: a magnet and color cannot separate nickel silver from plated brass, and either mislabel yields the wrong strike

failure_modes: trusting a hallmark alone when counterfeits exist
treating zinc die-cast as brass and dissolving detail in an acid step
spot-testing an heirloom without documented consent
acceptance_tests: the substrate class is recorded with at least one piece of physical evidence beyond the customer's claim; unknowns are escalated to the customer, never defaulted to brass
revisit_triggers: an adhesion or tarnish failure pattern clusters on one claimed substrate class
XRF or a consented spot test contradicts the intake claim

base.update_signal: shop XRF or assay outcomes overturning the bench heuristics for a substrate class

nodes.definition: Assign each piece a wear class before choosing gold build or topcoat, because abrasion exposure — not appearance — is what the stack must survive: rings and bracelets live in a rubbing, knocking, sweat-and-soap environment; pendants, brooches, and earring drops hang mostly untouched; posts and hooks barely abrade but press against skin, making them compliance-heavy and wear-light; clasps and daily-handled parts sit at the top of the abrasion ladder. The class drives three choices at once: the gold thickness band (flash versus heavy build), whether abrasion is carried by a hard gold class or by a topcoat, and what wear expectation is disclosed to the buyer in writing before sale.

included: wear-class ladder by use, not by piece name
excluded: delivering the thickness the class demands (electrical KB)
numeric wear-life promises stated as guarantees

pros.claim: One classification collapses the build-versus-topcoat debate into a lookup
pros.example: a pendant can honestly ship as sealed flash while the same design sold as a ring cannot

cons.claim: Real wear varies wildly by wearer and the class is a central tendency
cons.example: a desk worker's ring and a gardener's identical ring do not see the same year of abrasion

failure_modes: classifying by piece name instead of actual use
letting price rather than wear class set the build
shipping without a disclosed wear expectation
acceptance_tests: every job carries a wear class and a drafted wear-expectation disclosure before the gold build class is chosen
revisit_triggers: warranty returns cluster inside one wear class, indicating a misdrawn class boundary

base.update_signal: warranty-return rates by wear class from the shop log contradicting the class boundaries

nodes.definition: The rule that every layer in the stack comes from a purchased commercial plating system operated inside its supplier technical data sheet, and that numbers live in exactly three places: the TDS (setpoints), the shop's own logged runs (refinements), and published handbooks (cited as handbook-class ranges, never as shop setpoints). This KB therefore specifies stacks as layer classes with verification hooks — sulfamate-class ductile nickel, thickness per stack spec, run per TDS — and never as bath recipes. The node also carries the safety frame the chemistry demands: cyanide-complexed systems (some gold strikes, copper strikes, and white bronze types) are never mixed with, stored with, or drained with acids; ventilation, PPE, labeling, and training are obligation classes with the destination jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules verified rather than assumed; and DIY formulation from raw chemicals is excluded outright.

included: three-home rule for numbers (TDS, shop log, handbook classes)
cyanide/acid segregation as an obligation class
excluded: running titrations and replenishment (chemistry specialist)
writing safety procedure content beyond obligation classes and formal-training pointers

pros.claim: TDS governance keeps stack designs portable across suppliers and defensible in a dispute
pros.example: swapping one supplier's white bronze for another's changes the TDS reference on the run sheet, not the architecture

cons.claim: TDS windows constrain design freedom
cons.example: a barrier class the architecture wants may not be sold in a small-shop-compatible system at all

failure_modes: copying a handbook range onto a run sheet as if it were the product's setpoint
improvised additions to a proprietary bath
cyanide and acid lines sharing storage or a drain
acceptance_tests: every layer on a run sheet names a commercial product and its TDS; no setpoint appears that is not traceable to that TDS or to the shop's logged history; the storage plan shows cyanide/acid segregation
revisit_triggers: a supplier revises a TDS or safety data sheet for any system in the stack catalog
a new chemistry class enters the shop

base.update_signal: a TDS revision or hazard reclassification for any commercial system the stack catalog references

nodes.definition: The mechanism that kills thin gold on the bench's two favorite substrates: atoms move through thin deposits at room temperature over weeks to months. Silver migrates through thin gold and sulfides at the surface, so an unbarriered gold flash over sterling looks tarnished even though gold itself does not tarnish; copper and zinc from brass do the same, reading as brown-pink dulling and, with zinc, as haze. The rate scales with temperature, gold thinness and porosity, and time — which is why the complaint arrives after the sale rather than at final inspection. The countermeasure is architectural, not electrical: an adequate barrier class between a migrating substrate and the gold, or a gold build heavy enough to slow the path, plus the honesty to disclose the clock in writing when a customer declines the barrier.

included: solid-state migration of Ag, Cu, Zn through thin gold
excluded: bath contamination diagnosis (chemistry specialist)
quantified diffusion-rate predictions stated as fact

pros.claim: One mechanism explains an entire complaint family from the stack drawing alone
pros.example: a tarnished-gold complaint on a flashed sterling ring is diagnosed from the missing barrier line without touching a bath test

cons.claim: The mechanism is invisible at ship time, so discipline must run on theory rather than inspection
cons.example: two pieces, with and without barrier, are indistinguishable at final QC and months apart in the field

failure_modes: blaming the gold bath for a migration complaint
omitting the barrier on quick-refresh jobs because the last coat looked fine
assuming a topcoat substitutes for a barrier against migration from below
acceptance_tests: every stack over silver, brass, or copper either includes a named barrier layer class or carries a written customer disclosure that the finish is decorative and short-lived
revisit_triggers: tarnish-through complaints on stacks that included the specified barrier class
a new migrating substrate class enters the shop's intake

base.update_signal: field returns showing tarnish-through despite the specified barrier class and thickness class

nodes.definition: Thin gold is cathodic to nearly everything beneath it, so every pore, scratch-through, and wear spot becomes a small galvanic cell in which the base metal corrodes preferentially — the deposit's own nobility turned against its defects. Pore density falls as deposits thicken and as the underplate levels and seals the surface, which is why porosity of the finished stack is dominated by underplate quality more than by the gold itself. The bench consequences: a flash coat needs either a pore-blocking underplate or a sealing topcoat to survive sweat and salt; porosity testing (nitric-vapor class methods) belongs in the verification plan for skin-and-sweat wear classes; and a corrosion bloom at a pore is diagnostic evidence about the layer under the gold, not about the gold bath.

excluded: current-density causes of poor coverage (electrical KB)
running the porosity test procedure itself

pros.claim: The mechanism redirects corrosion diagnosis to the responsible layer
pros.example: green spotting on a flashed brass piece reads as pore-path corrosion of the brass, indicting a thin or absent underplate rather than the gold

cons.claim: Porosity is statistical and its test methods are class-level, so a pass is probabilistic
cons.example: a piece can pass a porosity check and still grow a wear-through cell at the one high spot the rack rubbed

failure_modes: sweat-class piece released with no pore strategy at all
interpreting pore bloom as bad gold and re-plating over the same defective underplate
porosity test skipped because the color looked right
acceptance_tests: every sweat-exposed wear class carries a pore strategy — underplate quality, gold build, or sealing topcoat — named in the stack drawing
revisit_triggers: porosity-test failures or field corrosion on a stack whose drawing claimed a pore strategy

base.update_signal: porosity-test outcomes correlated with underplate class and thickness in the shop log

nodes.definition: When a less-noble metal enters a solution of a more-noble one without current, the substrate dissolves and the noble metal displacement-plates as a dark, spongy, zero-adhesion film — the classic ruined-part mechanism when bare steel or zinc touches an acid gold or acid copper bath. Once an immersion film forms, everything plated over it inherits the non-bond and peels as a sheet. The stack-design counters are structural: a strike chosen so each bath in the sequence sees a compatible surface, live entry flagged at sensitive interfaces, and a layer order that never asks a reactive substrate to meet a noble-metal bath directly. The wiring and rectifier practice that implement live entry belong to the electrical and fixturing KBs; this node owns knowing where in the stack the hazard lives and drawing it on the stack diagram.

included: displacement mechanism and its nobility logic
interface compatibility audit of the stack sequence
excluded: executing live entry at the rectifier (electrical KB)
contact wiring practice (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: One nobility rule predicts an entire failure family before any tank is filled
pros.example: the stack drawing itself shows that zinc die-cast into an acid copper leveling bath is a forbidden interface

cons.claim: Over-applying the guard adds strike tanks a simple job never needed
cons.example: brass entering a cyanide-class gold strike is already a compatible interface without an extra strike in front of it

failure_modes: an it-is-only-in-for-a-second immersion dip that seeds a peeling sheet
re-plating an assembled piece whose solder joint or steel pin is the reactive member nobody audited
trusting rinse water to protect an active surface between tanks
acceptance_tests: the stack drawing marks every bath-entry interface as compatible, struck, or live-entry-flagged before the sequence is approved
revisit_triggers: a peeling-sheet failure on an interface the stack drawing had marked compatible

base.update_signal: a whole-stack peel traced to an interface the compatibility audit had cleared

nodes.definition: Choose the thin, adhesion-first layer each substrate needs before any build layer: Wood's-nickel-class strike for stainless and passive or aged nickel, whose high-acid, low-efficiency deposition strips the reforming passive film and lays fresh bonded nickel in the same instant; copper-strike class for mild steel and zinc alloys ahead of acid baths, with the alkaline non-cyanide copper class preferred at small-shop scale over the traditional cyanide type; and nickel- or gold-strike entries for brass and copper where the next bath demands them. A strike is deliberately thin — a strike-class film, not a build — runs at low cathodic efficiency, and exists to make the next layer's bond, not to add thickness or color. Executing the cleaning chain that precedes it belongs to the prep specialist; this node owns which strike, on what metal, and why.

excluded: strike bath make-up and analysis (chemistry specialist, per TDS)
the cleaning and pickling chain before the strike (prep specialist)

pros.claim: The strike decision is the cheapest insurance in the whole stack
pros.example: a Wood's-class strike line item turns stainless from an adhesion gamble into a routine substrate

cons.claim: Every strike adds a tank, a rinse, and a hazard class to manage
cons.example: adding a cyanide-class copper strike to a shop with acid-only drains is a safety-architecture problem, not a convenience

failure_modes: strike skipped on previously-plated nickel that has aged and passivated
a strike run so long it becomes a stressed build layer
a strike family incompatible with the bath that follows it
acceptance_tests: each substrate class in the stack catalog maps to a named strike class or a documented no-strike justification, and a bend or wrap adhesion coupon passes on the strike-bearing stack
revisit_triggers: adhesion failures cluster on one substrate-strike pairing
a strike product's TDS changes

base.update_signal: an adhesion-coupon failure pattern on a substrate the strike map calls covered

nodes.definition: The thin gold strike between the underplate and the main gold bath earns its tank twice over: it deposits an adherent gold film on nickel or other underplate surfaces that may have micro-passivated during transfer (adhesion duty), and it takes the drag-in hit so the expensive main gold bath does not (bath-protection duty — the strike is the sacrificial contamination buffer at the noble end of the line, exactly as the activation dip is at the base end). It matters most when the underplate is nickel, which passivates within a rinse delay; when the main bath is an acid gold intolerant of metallic drag-in; and when job flow makes pauses between tanks unavoidable. Skipping it on a fast, fresh, live-transferred line can be legitimate — as a documented per-job-class decision, never as a habit that spreads.

included: drag-in buffer duty for the main gold bath
excluded: gold strike bath chemistry and replenishment (chemistry specialist)
transfer timing execution (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: One thin layer protects both adhesion and the costliest bath in the shop simultaneously
pros.example: a matte, peelable gold-on-nickel result after a lunch-break pause is precisely the failure the strike line prevents

cons.claim: It is one more precious-metal bath to maintain, analyze, and inventory
cons.example: a rarely-used gold strike still ties up gold stock and bench space while it ages

failure_modes: nickel passivation during a rinse delay bridged by no strike
the strike bath quietly becoming the main deposit as dwell times drift
a skip decision made once and silently generalized to every job
acceptance_tests: every job class either includes the gold strike or carries a documented skip decision naming the fast-transfer condition that justifies it
revisit_triggers: adhesion or contamination trends in the main gold bath after upstream flow changes

base.update_signal: logged adhesion comparisons between struck and unstruck transfers on the shop's own line

nodes.definition: Nickel underplating treated as a class with internal choices, all run per TDS: Watts-type, the standard levelable barrier that brightens well; sulfamate-type, the near-zero-stress ductile choice when the piece will be formed after plating; and bright nickel, whose sulfur-bearing brightener chemistry levels beautifully and embrittles the deposit. As a barrier the class blocks iron and copper-family migration into thin gold, levels the surface (cutting final-stack porosity), and carries corrosion duty a sub-micron gold coat cannot. The non-negotiable attached to the whole class: nickel anywhere in a skin-contact stack triggers the nickel-release compliance gate, and the barrier choice is not complete until that gate has answered. Bath maintenance and analysis belong to the chemistry specialist; this node owns when nickel belongs in the stack and which nickel type.

included: Watts, sulfamate, and bright nickel as design classes
mandatory hand-off to the compliance gate for skin contact
excluded: nickel bath analysis and replenishment (chemistry specialist)
asserted numeric release limits (compliance node handles the regulation class)

pros.claim: Nickel is the most capable all-around barrier the bench can buy
pros.example: a steel piece with a Watts-class layer under gold passes the porosity check the same piece fails bare

cons.claim: Nickel is a skin sensitizer with regulated release limits, casting a compliance shadow over every jewelry use
cons.example: a technically perfect nickel-barriered earring can still be an unsellable product in a nickel-regulated market

failure_modes: bright nickel chosen for a piece later resized, cracking at the bend
a barrier specified with no compliance check attached
nickel type and thickness class left unstated on the run sheet
acceptance_tests: every nickel-bearing stack names the nickel type, a thickness class, and shows the compliance gate's verdict before release
revisit_triggers: skin-contact status or destination market changes on a catalog item
a forming step is added after plating on any nickel-bearing stack

base.update_signal: nickel-release test outcomes or regulation changes affecting where the class remains admissible

nodes.definition: The gate every skin-contact stack passes before nickel may stay in it. Jurisdictions with nickel-release rules — the EU's REACH-class restriction with its EN 1811 test class and EN 12472 wear-simulation class is the anchor example — limit how much nickel a worn article may release, and release is a property of the finished stack, not of any bath: a sound gold-plus-topcoat over nickel can pass while the same nickel under worn-through flash fails. The gate's questions: does the piece contact skin (piercing-post parts are the strictest class); which market does it ship to; can the finished stack demonstrate compliance by test, or should the design simply go nickel-free. This KB never asserts the numeric limits — it names them as regulation classes and requires verifying current rules in the destination jurisdiction. Customer allergy questions route to regulation classes and professional medical care, never to bench diagnosis.

included: regulation classes named without asserted numbers
excluded: performing the release test (external lab class)
medical advice on nickel allergy
marketing-term rules (the terms node owns those)

pros.claim: The gate converts a legal hazard into a routine one-step design decision
pros.example: an order line reading EU earring resolves to nickel-free-by-default with no test burden at all

cons.claim: Compliance-by-test is slow and priced beyond one-off jobs
cons.example: an EN-1811-class test on a single custom bracelet can cost more than the job itself

failure_modes: treating release compliance as a bath property instead of a stack property
a hypoallergenic claim made with nickel anywhere in the stack
relying on remembered limit numbers instead of the current regulation text
acceptance_tests: no nickel-bearing skin-contact stack ships without either a documented compliance basis for the destination market or a redesign to nickel-free; claim wording is checked against the regulation class
revisit_triggers: regulation text or enforcement guidance changes in a destination market
wear-through is observed on a stack whose compliance rested on an intact gold-plus-topcoat

base.update_signal: a change in nickel-release regulation text or enforcement guidance in any destination market the shop serves

nodes.definition: The two commercial nickel-free barrier classes that replace nickel when compliance or allergy takes it off the table, each with a real bill. Palladium class — pure Pd or Pd-alloy strike-barrier run per TDS on insoluble anodes — is a noble thin-flash barrier that blocks diffusion at minimum thickness, but pure palladium absorbs hydrogen and microcracks when plated thick or fast, so it is a flash-class layer by design, and precious-metal price exposure rides on every job. White bronze class — a Cu-Sn-Zn alloy from proprietary systems, traditionally cyanide-complexed with cyanide-free versions on the market — is a bright-white, tarnish-resistant, hard barrier, but harder and less ductile than nickel (a poor partner for post-plate forming), and its alloy ratio drifts with operating conditions, making it an analysis-heavy bath that belongs with a supplier's TDS and analysis service. Choosing between them is wear class plus forming plan plus cost structure, never preference.

included: palladium-class flash barriers with the thick-build veto
white bronze class with its ductility and analysis bills
selection logic by wear, forming, and cost
excluded: white bronze bath analysis itself (supplier service plus chemistry specialist)
asserted alloy ratios or setpoints beyond class descriptions

pros.claim: The classes make the compliant stack buildable rather than aspirational
pros.example: an EU-bound sterling ring gets a palladium-flash-class barrier under its gold and passes the skin-contact question by design

cons.claim: Both classes cost more per micron or per analysis than nickel, and each carries a mechanical veto
cons.example: white bronze under a bangle that will be re-shaped cracks exactly where bright nickel would have

failure_modes: palladium plated thick for safety and microcracking from absorbed hydrogen
white bronze color and brittleness drifting off-class unnoticed between analyses
a cyanide-type white bronze adopted into a shop whose safety plan was built acid-only
acceptance_tests: nickel-free stacks name the barrier class, its thickness class, and the forming verdict; white-bronze runs show a supplier analysis arrangement on record
revisit_triggers: a supplier discontinues or reformulates a nickel-free system
a precious-metal price move changes the default barrier economics

base.update_signal: bend-coupon and tarnish outcomes from the shop's own nickel-free runs

nodes.definition: Copper's role in the stack is geometry, not protection: a ductile, fast-building, inexpensive layer that levels scratches and casting texture, takes a high polish before the next layer, and cushions mechanical mismatch between substrate and barrier — the classic base for heavy builds where the piece needs re-surfacing that would be unaffordable in nickel and unthinkable in gold. Its hard limit is equally architectural: copper is itself a migrator, so it must never be the layer directly under thin gold — a barrier always sits between copper and the gold above it. On steel and zinc the copper goes on over a strike, never directly into an acid copper bath, and a heavy copper build exists to be polished — an unpolished leveling layer is just thickness that cost money.

excluded: copper bath types and their chemistry control (chemistry specialist)
the polishing operation itself (finishing bench)

pros.claim: Copper buys surface quality per unit cost that nothing else in the stack matches
pros.example: a pitted cast brass buckle becomes mirror-flat under copper plus polish before a thin barrier and flash finish it

cons.claim: It adds a polish step and a migration source if the stack above it is designed lazily
cons.example: copper directly under flash gold reads warm for a month and then dull brown as the copper comes through

failure_modes: copper-under-gold with no intervening barrier
acid copper asked to deposit directly on zinc or bare steel
a leveling build specified but the polish step dropped from the router
acceptance_tests: every copper layer in a drawing shows a strike beneath it on reactive substrates and a barrier above it before any gold
revisit_triggers: warm-then-brown color complaints on stacks that carried copper near the gold

base.update_signal: surface-quality comparisons between the shop's copper-leveled and direct-barrier runs

nodes.definition: Layered systems beat one thick layer because each interface interrupts defects and each layer can specialize: duplex nickel as a class (semi-bright under bright) staggers corrosion paths so a pore through one layer dead-ends at the next; copper-then-barrier pairs a ductile leveler with a migration blocker; barrier-then-gold-strike-then-gold gives adhesion, protection, and color each their own layer; hard-gold-over-soft or gold-over-palladium-flash tunes wear and cost independently. The designer's discipline: every layer must have a named job and a thickness class — a layer nobody can justify is drag-out cost, tank time, and failure surface. And multi-layer multiplies interfaces, every one of which is an adhesion risk that must be owned by a strike, an activation, or a live transfer.

included: duplex nickel and multi-layer composition patterns
excluded: delivering each layer's thickness (electrical KB)
transfer execution between tanks (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: Engineered redundancy survives the defect a single layer feeds straight to the substrate
pros.example: a duplex-nickel-class stack under gold outlasts a single layer of equal total thickness in sweat exposure because pores dead-end at the interlayer

cons.claim: Each layer adds tanks, transfer risk, and process cost
cons.example: a five-layer architecture on a low-price fashion piece can cost more in process time than the piece earns back

failure_modes: layers accreting by habit with no named job
interface count outrunning the shop's transfer discipline
celebrating total thickness while a single unowned interface fails adhesion
acceptance_tests: every layer in the stack drawing carries a named job and thickness class, and every interface names its adhesion owner — strike, activation, or live transfer
revisit_triggers: verification failures localized to a specific interface
a new wear-class requirement enters the catalog

base.update_signal: field-failure comparisons between the shop's single-layer and duplex or multi-layer stacks

nodes.definition: The gold budget decision: a flash — a color-only class of coat that exists for appearance and pricing, not wear — versus a heavy build class that puts real gold in the wear path. The mapping runs from wear class: hang-only pieces can be honest flash with a barrier and, where chosen, a sealing topcoat; rub-and-knock classes need build (usually with a hard gold top or a film topcoat) or an explicit, disclosed short-life positioning; skin-contact compliance can impose thickness logic of its own through the release gate. Two mechanisms bound the flash end: below a tint-through threshold class the white of a barrier reads through and cools the color, and porosity rises as gold thins. Delivering whatever thickness this node targets — the amperes, minutes, and area math — is the electrical KB's job; this node sets the target class and owns the honesty of the promise attached to it.

included: tint-through and porosity limits of the flash end
written disclosure duty on the thin end
excluded: Faraday-based delivery math and verification by XRF or coupon at run time (electrical KB)
numeric thickness guarantees stated as universal fact

pros.claim: The mapping matches gold spend to what the piece actually endures
pros.example: one wear-class table prices a pendant as flash and its companion ring as build, both honestly

cons.claim: The honest build is sometimes unsellable at the customer's price point
cons.example: a customer wanting a durable ring at flash price forces a disclosure conversation, not a thicker lie

failure_modes: a ring-class piece shipped as undisclosed flash
thickness promised in microns nobody will ever measure
flash pushed below the tint-through class over a white barrier to save gold
acceptance_tests: the gold build class per wear class is recorded on the run sheet with the disclosed wear expectation, and sub-tint-through flash is never specified over white barriers without a color check
revisit_triggers: measured thickness repeatedly missing the class target
wear complaints arriving in a class the table calls covered

base.update_signal: XRF-verified build outcomes and wear-return data by class accumulating in the shop log

nodes.definition: Choosing what the visible gold actually is: a soft high-karat-color class — the richest yellow and the softest surface a stack can end in — versus a hardened acid-gold class alloyed for wear at some color cost, versus a karat-toned alloy class chosen to match an existing piece. Color is a stack property near the flash end: below the tint-through class a white barrier cools the tone, and the same gold over palladium-white and over yellow brass do not read identical, so matching a customer's set means matching the whole visible stack against a retained reference under consistent light. What this node refuses to do: fake richness with tinted topcoats or thickness claims — gold-tinted e-coat exists as a color-correction class and is usable only with honest labeling, a decision that lives with the topcoat and terms nodes.

included: soft color gold versus hard gold versus toned alloy classes
excluded: gold bath formulation and karat chemistry control (chemistry specialist)
tinted-coat labeling rules (terms node)

pros.claim: Separating the wear decision from the color decision keeps either from being compromised blind
pros.example: a hard-gold top for the clasp and a high-karat color coat for the matching pendant, each from its own line of the same architecture

cons.claim: Color judgment is perceptual and lighting-dependent
cons.example: a piece matched under bench LEDs reads greener in daylight beside the customer's older vermeil

failure_modes: a soft high-karat surface on a wear-class piece with no hard layer or topcoat behind the decision
color matched from memory instead of a retained reference
tone drift blamed on the bath when it is tint-through from a thinning flash
acceptance_tests: color-match jobs are checked against a retained reference under the shop's standard light before release
revisit_triggers: customer color rejections on jobs the reference practice had passed

base.update_signal: customer color-acceptance outcomes against the retained-reference matching practice

nodes.definition: The naming gate between the stack and the sales channel: gold plated, vermeil, gold filled, rolled gold, and their kin are regulated term classes whose definitions — substrate condition, minimum gold thickness, karat floors, bonding method — vary by jurisdiction and change over time, so the discipline is that the term follows the verified stack, never the reverse, and current rules in the destination market are checked rather than recalled. Hard lines that never move: plated goods are never represented as solid gold; vermeil-class terms require the silver-substrate condition of the governing rule, not a brass piece with wishful naming; gold filled and rolled gold describe bonded-metal constructions a plating tank cannot produce, so an electroplated stack never wears them; wear expectations are disclosed before sale; heirloom risk is documented at intake. The seller's term intent arrives in the brief, and the run sheet may not carry a term the stack cannot support.

included: term classes and their stack conditions
excluded: asserted numeric thickness thresholds for any term
drafting the listing copy itself
nickel-release rules (compliance node)

pros.claim: The gate keeps the shop out of misrepresentation and relabel-and-refund disputes
pros.example: refusing vermeil on a brass piece at quote time costs one conversation; the same refusal after sale costs the customer relationship

cons.claim: Honest terms can lose a sale to a looser competitor
cons.example: the customer who wanted the word vermeil more than the silver substrate walks to whoever will print it

failure_modes: a term chosen at listing time with no stack evidence behind it
electroplated goods labeled gold filled
jurisdiction differences ignored on export sales
acceptance_tests: every marketing term on a quote or listing maps to a stack property that supports it under the destination market's current rule class, and no representation implies solid gold for a plated piece
revisit_triggers: a destination market's term definitions change
a marketplace platform adds its own term policy on top of the regulation class

base.update_signal: a rule-class or marketplace-policy change governing any term the shop uses

nodes.definition: The invisible end of the topcoat spectrum: chemisorbed molecular films that block tarnish chemistry without changing look or feel. Benzotriazole-class films complex with copper- and silver-bearing surfaces — including the copper and nickel exposed at the pores of thin gold — and are the museum and electronics classic; proprietary thiol or SAM passivate dips bond to gold, silver, nickel, and copper, add hydrophobicity and sweat resistance, and are the jewelry trade's standard drop-in replacement for legacy hexavalent-chromate passivates, which this KB excludes outright as a carcinogen class. Molecular films flex with the metal, surviving forming that would crack any hard coat, cost almost nothing per piece, and renew easily — and they are monolayer-thin: they slow chemistry at pores, they do not armor against abrasion, and they never substitute for a barrier against migration from below.

included: BTA-class and thiol/SAM-class passivates as classes
excluded: dip bath concentration and maintenance (per product TDS)
abrasion protection claims of any kind

pros.claim: Protection with zero look-and-feel cost
pros.example: a bare-gold-feel pendant over sterling gets a SAM-class dip and resists the sweat tarnish it would otherwise show at pores

cons.claim: No wear protection and a finite service life
cons.example: the same dip on a daily ring is rubbed through in weeks, so the customer must never have been sold protected without that clock disclosed

failure_modes: a passivate sold as scratch protection
the dip applied over fingerprints, sealing the soil in
a legacy chromate-class product accepted from old stock
acceptance_tests: every passivate line on a run sheet names a chromate-free commercial product and pairs the sale with a disclosed protection scope — tarnish, not abrasion
revisit_triggers: supplier reformulation of the passivate dip or adverse sweat-test outcomes on treated pieces

base.update_signal: supplier reformulation notices or the shop's own sweat-exposure comparisons on dipped versus undipped pieces

nodes.definition: The visible-film end of post-plate protection, chosen as classes with known bills: e-coat clear — electrophoretic waterborne lacquer, DC-deposited, self-limiting, uniform into recesses, then oven-cured; the mass-market mechanism behind long-lived fashion gold, available gold-tinted for color correction that is honest only with labeling; sol-gel ceramic hybrids — the scratch-hardness champion among wet-applied clears, thin and glass-brittle; and the conventional lacquer classes — acrylic (museum-reversible), nitrocellulose (historic, yellowing, very flammable), 2K polyurethane (toughest, isocyanate hazard class), UV-acrylate (fast, needs UV equipment). Every film buys tarnish and scratch protection by trading away bare-metal feel and adding a cure step and an aging or yellowing clock, and every film is a last step applied to the finished, formed shape — cured films crack and peel at forming strains. Selection is wear class plus geometry plus shop equipment plus disclosure, each product run per its TDS with its ventilation and hazard classes respected.

included: e-coat, sol-gel, and lacquer classes with their trade-off bills
excluded: cure schedules and bath parameters (per each product's TDS)
PVD and other dry-process caps (different equipment class, cross-referenced not covered)

pros.claim: Films extend flash-class finishes into wear classes they could never survive bare
pros.example: e-coat over flash on a fashion bangle is the difference between a season of wear and a fortnight

cons.claim: Plastic feel, an aging clock, and cure infrastructure come with every film
cons.example: an amber-shifted clear on a white-finished piece is a worse complaint than the tarnish it prevented

failure_modes: a film applied before forming or sizing and cracking at the strain line
overbake ambering read as a bath fault
a tinted coat used to fake karat richness without labeling
an isocyanate-class product used without its ventilation obligation class
acceptance_tests: the topcoat class is chosen against wear class and geometry with cure equipment confirmed on hand, and tinted variants carry a labeling sign-off
revisit_triggers: yellowing or delamination returns clustering on one coated class

base.update_signal: coating-failure returns by class in the shop log or a TDS or hazard reclassification for a film product

nodes.definition: Whether the stack will survive what happens to the piece after plating. Stack ductility is set by the underplate, not the gold: additive-free sulfamate-class nickel is the near-zero-stress ductile member; Watts semi-bright sits mid-pack; bright sulfur-carrying nickel and white bronze are the brittle members that crack at bends and radiate the crack through every layer above; hard films — sol-gel, cured e-coat, PVD-class caps — tolerate wear flex but not forming strain. The decision tree: if sizing, bending, or coiling happens after plating, the stack is built from the ductile column and hard topcoats are deferred until after forming — or the operation is re-sequenced to form first and plate after. Generous bend radii help but never license a brittle stack into a known bend. Hydrogen embrittlement of spring-steel substrates is flagged here as a class and handed to the prep-and-bake practice that owns it.

excluded: the bake procedure for hydrogen relief (prep specialist)
the forming operation itself (jeweler's bench)

pros.claim: The fit check prevents the cruellest rework — a perfect finish destroyed by the first sizing
pros.example: a ring band planned for post-plate sizing gets a sulfamate-class barrier and no hard clear until after the size

cons.claim: The ductile column gives up hardness and leveling brilliance
cons.example: choosing sulfamate over bright nickel costs the mirror leveling the customer admired on the sample

failure_modes: a brittle barrier discovered at the sizing bench
a hard topcoat applied before a known forming step
the forming question never asked at intake
acceptance_tests: every job with a post-plate forming step carries a ductile-column stack or a documented re-sequenced plan
revisit_triggers: cracking at bends on any stack the ductility table calls safe

base.update_signal: bend-coupon results across the shop's underplate classes contradicting the ductility ranking

nodes.definition: The acceptance plan written into the stack design rather than bolted on after: adhesion by bend, wrap, or heat-quench coupon (ASTM-B571-class options) at the strike stage and on the finished stack; per-layer thickness by XRF (ISO-3497 and ASTM-B568 class) with microsection as the referee class; porosity testing (nitric-vapor class) for sweat wear classes; nickel-release testing (EN-1811 class with EN-12472 wear simulation) whenever nickel remains in a skin-contact stack; and a witness coupon racked with the job when the piece itself cannot be tested. Each check names its layer and its pass basis, and each failure routes to the layer that owns it — adhesion to strike and substrate, porosity to underplate, color to the visible stack. Not owned here: run-time delivery measurement (the electrical KB verifies microns against amperes and minutes) and run-logging mechanics (fixturing KB); this is the stack-level definition of done.

included: per-layer check catalog as test classes
excluded: run-time thickness delivery verification (electrical KB)
log storage and traceability mechanics (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: The plan converts looks-good into evidence per layer
pros.example: a wrap-test coupon catches weak strike adhesion before any gold is spent on a doomed build

cons.claim: Coupons and per-layer checks cost time and imperfectly represent complex geometry
cons.example: a flat coupon passes while the recessed filigree the rack shadowed fails in the field

failure_modes: verification defined after plating instead of before
a coupon material that does not match the job's substrate
the nickel-release check skipped because the gold covers it
acceptance_tests: the verification plan exists before the first tank and names a check, a layer, and a pass basis for every layer class in the stack
revisit_triggers: any field return on a stack that passed its plan — the plan itself, not only the piece, becomes the suspect

base.update_signal: correlation between plan-passing stacks and field returns accumulating in the shop log

nodes.definition: The written artifact that turns the architecture into an executable run: layer order with a job and thickness class per layer; the commercial product and TDS reference per bath; strike and live-entry flags at sensitive interfaces; the compliance verdicts — nickel release and term support — attached; the verification plan's hooks (which coupon, which XRF points); and the disclosed wear expectation as sold. It is the handoff boundary to the sibling KBs: electrical delivery (surface area, current density, time) and physical execution (racking, contacts, rinse sequence, logging) both execute from this sheet, and the run log they return is what refines the shop's stack templates over time. A stack that lives only in the plater's head is not a stack; it is a liability with good intentions.

included: handoff boundary to the electrical and fixturing KBs
excluded: computing electrical parameters (electrical KB)
executing and archiving the log (fixturing KB)

pros.claim: The sheet makes the stack reproducible by someone other than its author
pros.example: a repeat order six months later replays the sheet instead of re-deriving the stack from a memory of the piece

cons.claim: Sheets ossify if nobody curates them
cons.example: a template kept after a supplier change quietly points at a TDS the shop no longer owns

failure_modes: layer order left implicit between bath names
thickness classes missing so the electrical KB has no target
compliance verdicts not attached so the term gate is bypassed at listing time
acceptance_tests: a second qualified operator can execute the run from the sheet alone; every bath line carries a TDS reference; compliance verdicts and verification hooks are attached
revisit_triggers: any execution question from the electrical or fixturing side that the sheet cannot answer
a supplier or TDS change invalidating a template line

base.update_signal: handoff-friction reports from the electrical or fixturing side of the bench

edges.why_related: substrate identification starts from the claim and the evidence the brief captured
the wear class is assigned from the use and customer answers recorded in the brief
which migration mechanisms threaten the stack follows from which metal the substrate actually is
displacement risk is a property of the substrate's nobility against each bath in the sequence
how aggressively pores corrode depends on the substrate exposed at their bottom
the strike map exists to close the incompatible interfaces the displacement audit identifies
the barrier requirement the nickel class answers is set by the migration verdict
copper's own migrator status — and hence its never-directly-under-gold rule — comes from the migration mechanism
the flash-versus-build decision is the wear class translated into gold budget
the compliance gate is invoked the moment nickel enters the stack
the nickel-free classes are the design answer when the compliance gate rules nickel out
the gold strike is the noble-end entry of the same substrate-to-strike map
duplex and multi-layer architectures are composed from the barrier classes this node defines
the leveling layer is the ductile member the multi-layer patterns build on
which gold class tops the stack is chosen inside the build class already set
term admissibility depends on the gold build class the stack actually carries
the passivate's job description is written by the pore-cell mechanism it slows
film topcoats are the pore-sealing option the corrosion mechanism motivates
stack ductility is inherited from the underplate class chosen here
the verification plan enumerates checks per layer of the assembled architecture
the release-test class enters the plan whenever the compliance verdict requires proof
the run sheet carries the verification hooks; without the plan there is nothing complete to hand off
every bath line on the sheet must point at a commercial product's TDS
nickel types are specified as classes only; setpoints stay with the product TDS and the shop's logged history
no skin-contact architecture may rely on nickel anywhere in the stack without a compliance basis
the run sheet may not carry a marketing term the verified stack cannot support
hard films are barred until every forming operation on the piece is complete
the sales channel wants the richest term at the thinnest gold, while the term gate accepts only what the stack verifies
edges.resolution_rule: the term follows the measured stack under the destination market's rule class; when the desired term and the affordable build disagree, either the build rises or the term changes — the listing never overrules the stack

edges.why_related: nickel is the cheaper, more ductile, better-leveling barrier; nickel-free is the compliant and hypoallergenic one
edges.resolution_rule: for skin-contact pieces bound for a nickel-release jurisdiction, nickel-free wins regardless of cost or finish preference; nickel stays only with a documented compliance basis — safety and compliance beat cost every time they meet

edges.why_related: the film armors but changes feel and ages; the molecular film preserves feel but cannot armor
edges.resolution_rule: wear class decides: rub-and-knock classes get a film or a hard gold build, while hang-only and premium bare-feel pieces get a molecular passivate with the shorter protection clock disclosed in writing

edges.why_related: the wear-optimal architecture wants hard bright layers exactly where the forming plan needs ductile ones
edges.resolution_rule: if forming after plating is fixed in the brief, the ductile column wins and hardness is recovered by re-sequencing (form first) or by a post-forming topcoat — a brittle stack never ships into a known bend

edges.why_related: thinning the gold raises through-porosity, multiplying the pore cells the corrosion mechanism feeds on
adding copper to the stack adds a migrator: an unbarriered copper layer becomes the source that discolors thin gold above it
a misidentified substrate propagates directly into the wrong strike and from there into whole-stack adhesion failure
the strike is deposited immediately before the underplate, and the transfer window between them must not allow repassivation
the passivate dip follows the final gold rinse directly, before first dry handling can deposit the fingerprints it would otherwise seal in
porosity and adhesion results feed back into which barrier class and thickness class the stack templates specify
logged run outcomes flow back to refine the intake questions and the default stack templates
both govern the first seconds of a bath interface — one with a sacrificial adherent film, the other by forbidding uncontrolled displacement in that same moment

conflict_axes.name: compliance_vs_barrier_economics
conflict_axes.description: Nickel is the cheapest and most capable barrier the bench can buy, and nickel-release rules make it a liability in skin-contact stacks bound for regulated markets.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: skin contact plus a regulated destination resolves to nickel-free by default; nickel stays only with a documented compliance basis for the finished stack

conflict_axes.name: flash_economics_vs_wear_honesty
conflict_axes.description: Thin flash maximizes margin per job while wear classes demand real build or an honestly disclosed short life.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the wear class sets the floor; below it, flash ships only with a written short-life disclosure the customer accepted

conflict_axes.name: bare_gold_feel_vs_film_protection
conflict_axes.description: Film topcoats protect flash finishes but trade away the bare-metal feel and add an aging clock; molecular passivates preserve feel but cannot armor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: assign by wear class and disclose the trade: films for rub-and-knock, molecular passivates with a disclosed clock for hang-only and premium-feel pieces

conflict_axes.name: hardness_vs_ductility
conflict_axes.description: Bright nickel, white bronze, and hard films serve wear resistance; sulfamate-class nickel and soft layers serve post-plate forming — the same stack cannot maximize both.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the forming plan in the brief decides: any post-plate forming locks the ductile column and defers hard members until after the bend

conflict_axes.name: leveling_gain_vs_migration_source
conflict_axes.description: Copper buys unmatched surface quality and polish base, and simultaneously adds a migrating metal the gold must be defended from.
poles: minimal migrator inventory in the stack
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use copper where surface economics justify it and always interpose a barrier before gold; where no leveling is needed, leave the migrator out

conflict_axes.name: stack_simplicity_vs_engineered_redundancy
conflict_axes.description: Fewer tanks and interfaces mean fewer adhesion risks and lower cost; layered redundancy interrupts corrosion paths a single layer feeds to the substrate.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add a layer only when it has a named job the wear class or substrate demands; refuse layers justified by habit

conflict_axes.name: throughput_vs_interface_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Skipping strikes, gold strikes, and coupons saves minutes per run and silently spends adhesion and bath health.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: skips are allowed only as documented per-job-class decisions with a named justifying condition, never as habits

conflict_axes.name: handbook_prior_vs_tds_authority
conflict_axes.description: Published handbook-class ranges tempt the bench as ready-made setpoints, while the commercial product's TDS and the shop's own log are the only legitimate number sources.
poles: TDS and shop log as setpoint
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: handbooks teach mechanisms and classes; the run sheet cites only the TDS and logged history — a handbook number on a run sheet is a defect

conflict_axes.name: color_richness_vs_disclosure
conflict_axes.description: Tinted topcoats and stack tricks can make thin gold read richer than it is; honest labeling limits what the shop may simulate.
poles: color that matches the disclosed stack
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: color correction is legitimate only with labeling that survives scrutiny; richness may never simulate a thickness or karat claim the stack cannot support

conflict_axes.name: customer_desire_vs_escalation_duty
conflict_axes.description: The customer wants the piece plated anyway — heirloom, unknown substrate, or a geometry that cannot be contacted without damage — while the shop's duty is to escalate rather than force.
poles: escalate what the bench cannot honestly do
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: unknown substrates needing destructive tests, heirloom irreversibility, and undamageable-contact problems all route to a documented intake/customer decision; the bench never forces them

edge_cases.description: A customer requests a quick gold flash directly over a sterling silver ring with no barrier
edge_cases.trigger: flash-over-silver order with barrier declined or unpriced
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the migration clock, quote the barriered stack as the default, and take the unbarriered job only with a written short-life disclosure

edge_cases.description: The piece is a mystery white metal, possibly previously plated, and the customer cannot say what it is
edge_cases.trigger: intake cannot assign a substrate class from non-destructive evidence
edge_cases.mitigation: treat as passive-prone (Wood's-class strike planning), use XRF where available, and escalate to the customer before any destructive spot test

edge_cases.description: An order form shows an EU destination and earring posts specified with bright nickel under the gold
edge_cases.trigger: skin-contact piece with nickel in the stack bound for a nickel-release jurisdiction
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to a palladium-class or white-bronze barrier, or hold the nickel stack until a compliance basis for the finished article exists; verify the current rules, never remembered numbers

edge_cases.description: The piece turns out to be zinc die-cast pot metal that acid baths will dissolve
edge_cases.trigger: substrate identified as zinc alloy after the stack was drafted around brass assumptions
edge_cases.mitigation: redesign the entry as alkaline-first with a non-cyanide copper-strike class per its TDS, and re-audit every later interface for displacement risk

edge_cases.description: The customer insists on the word vermeil for a gold-plated brass piece
edge_cases.trigger: a regulated term requested that the substrate condition cannot support
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the term, explain the silver-substrate condition of the term class, and offer the accurate class wording the stack does support

edge_cases.description: A ring will be resized after plating and the drafted stack uses bright nickel with a sol-gel topcoat
edge_cases.trigger: post-plate forming step discovered against a brittle stack column
edge_cases.mitigation: swap to the ductile column (sulfamate-class barrier), defer any hard film until after sizing, or re-sequence to form first and plate after

edge_cases.description: The white bronze barrier drifts off its alloy class and coupons crack on the bend test
edge_cases.trigger: yellowing or embrittlement signs on white-bronze-barriered work
edge_cases.mitigation: invoke the supplier analysis service, quarantine the class until the bath is back on TDS, and run a bend coupon with every batch in the interim

edge_cases.description: Gold plated straight onto a nickel underplate that sat in rinse water through a lunch break peels in a sheet
edge_cases.trigger: matte or peelable gold after a pause between nickel and gold tanks
edge_cases.mitigation: reactivate the nickel and add the gold-strike line for any flow with pauses; make skip decisions conditional on fast live transfer only

edge_cases.description: A palladium barrier is plated heavily for extra safety and microcracks from absorbed hydrogen
edge_cases.trigger: Pd thickness pushed beyond flash class
edge_cases.mitigation: keep palladium at its thin-flash class per TDS; where more barrier mass is genuinely needed, change class rather than thickening the Pd

edge_cases.description: A gold-tinted e-coat is proposed to make a pale flash read like a richer karat
edge_cases.trigger: color complaint answered with tint instead of stack correction
edge_cases.mitigation: allow tinted coats only with labeling sign-off; a tint may correct tone, never simulate a thickness or karat claim

edge_cases.description: A mixed-metal assembly arrives: silver shank, brass bezel, steel pin, one stack requested
edge_cases.trigger: multiple substrate classes in one piece
edge_cases.mitigation: design the strike plan to the most restrictive member, audit every member against every bath, and consider disassembly or a selective route via the fixturing KB escalation

edge_cases.description: An inherited piece is offered for plating and the stack would be near-irreversible on it
edge_cases.trigger: heirloom flagged at intake or discovered mid-design
edge_cases.mitigation: document the heirloom risk in writing, obtain explicit customer sign-off before design proceeds, and escalate rather than assume consent

workflow.description: Record substrate claim and evidence, wear and skin-contact answers, destination market, forming plan, term intent, and heirloom flag
workflow.gate: all brief fields present, heirloom sign-off obtained where flagged

workflow.action: Identify the substrate and its risk flags
workflow.description: Assign the substrate class from physical evidence and flag its migration, passivation, and acid-solubility risks
workflow.artifact: substrate class assignment with evidence note
workflow.gate: class assigned with evidence beyond the claim; unknowns escalated

workflow.description: Classify the piece by real abrasion exposure and draft the wear-expectation disclosure
workflow.artifact: wear class tag plus drafted disclosure
workflow.gate: class and disclosure recorded before any build decision

workflow.action: Rule on migration and pore mechanisms
workflow.description: Decide whether the substrate demands a barrier and whether the wear class demands a pore strategy, citing the mechanism
workflow.gate: barrier requirement decided yes or no with the mechanism cited

workflow.action: Audit bath-entry interfaces and choose strikes
workflow.description: Mark every interface compatible, struck, or live-entry-flagged and map each substrate to its strike class
workflow.gate: no unowned interface remains; skips carry documented justifications

workflow.description: Select nickel type or route to nickel-free, with thickness class and the compliance hand-off attached
workflow.gate: barrier named with thickness class; nickel choices carry the compliance invocation

workflow.description: Resolve skin contact and destination market into a compliance basis or a nickel-free redesign, verifying current rules
workflow.gate: no nickel remains in a skin-contact stack without a documented basis

workflow.action: Set the gold build and top layer
workflow.description: Translate the wear class into flash or build, pick the top gold class, and check the tint-through limit over white barriers
workflow.artifact: gold build class plus top-layer choice
workflow.gate: build matches wear class; disclosure drafted; term intent still supported

workflow.action: Select the topcoat class or none
workflow.description: Choose molecular passivate, film class, or bare finish against wear class, geometry, equipment, and feel expectations
workflow.gate: topcoat matches wear class and equipment; chromate classes excluded; tint carries labeling sign-off

workflow.description: Verify the stack column against any post-plate forming and re-sequence or swap to the ductile column where needed
workflow.gate: no brittle member or hard film precedes a known forming step

workflow.description: Name a check, a layer, and a pass basis for every layer class — adhesion coupons, per-layer XRF classes, porosity and release-test classes
workflow.gate: every layer has a check before the first tank; nickel stacks include the release-test class

workflow.description: Compose layer order, TDS references, entry flags, compliance verdicts, verification hooks, and the sold disclosure into the executable sheet
workflow.gate: a second qualified operator could execute from the sheet alone; every bath line cites a TDS

dominance_rules.rule: Compliance beats cost: a skin-contact piece bound for a nickel-release jurisdiction goes nickel-free unless a documented compliance basis exists
dominance_rules.rationale: an unsellable or unlawful article erases every saving the cheaper barrier made
dominance_rules.trigger: nickel proposed anywhere in a skin-contact stack
dominance_rules.action: route through the compliance gate; default to palladium-class or white-bronze barriers absent a basis

dominance_rules.rule: The verified stack beats the marketing term: naming follows measurement, never the reverse
dominance_rules.rationale: a term the stack cannot support is misrepresentation with a paper trail
dominance_rules.trigger: a listing term and the stack evidence disagree
dominance_rules.action: raise the build or change the term; never adjust the claim to the wish

dominance_rules.rule: The TDS and shop log beat handbook priors and bench folklore for every setpoint
dominance_rules.rationale: handbooks teach classes and mechanisms; only the product's TDS and logged runs describe the bath actually in the tank
dominance_rules.trigger: any number is about to be written onto a run sheet
dominance_rules.action: trace it to the TDS or the shop log or strike it

dominance_rules.rule: Interface integrity beats throughput: strikes and coupons are never skipped to save minutes
dominance_rules.rationale: one peeled stack costs more than a month of saved strike time
dominance_rules.trigger: schedule pressure proposes dropping a strike, gold strike, or coupon
dominance_rules.action: keep the interface owner; a skip requires a documented per-job-class justification

dominance_rules.rule: The mechanism verdict beats the customer request: unbarriered thin gold over a migrating substrate is refused or disclosed in writing
dominance_rules.rationale: the tarnish clock runs whether or not the customer believed in it
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer declines the barrier or the build the mechanism demands
dominance_rules.action: quote the honest stack; accept the thin job only with signed short-life disclosure

dominance_rules.rule: Ductility beats hardness when post-plate forming is fixed in the brief
dominance_rules.rationale: a cracked stack at the sizing bench is total rework plus a damaged piece
dominance_rules.trigger: a forming step exists after plating in the job plan
dominance_rules.action: build from the ductile column and defer hard members until after forming, or re-sequence to form first

dominance_rules.rule: Escalation beats force: unknown substrates needing destructive identification and heirloom irreversibility go to the customer, not the tank
dominance_rules.rationale: the shop can replate a finish but cannot un-etch an heirloom or un-guess a substrate
dominance_rules.trigger: identification requires destructive testing, or the piece is flagged irreplaceable
dominance_rules.action: stop design, document, and obtain an explicit intake/customer decision

dominance_rules.rule: Safety segregation beats convenience: no stack choice may put cyanide-class and acid chemistries into shared storage, handling, or drains
dominance_rules.rationale: the failure mode of that adjacency is lethal gas, not rework
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed layer class introduces a cyanide-type system into the line plan
dominance_rules.action: verify the segregation plan and jurisdiction rules before the class is adopted; otherwise choose the non-cyanide class

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure beats color trickery: tinted coats correct tone only under honest labeling
dominance_rules.rationale: a tint that simulates thickness or karat converts a color tool into a misrepresentation
dominance_rules.trigger: a tinted topcoat is proposed to answer a color complaint
dominance_rules.action: permit the tint only with the labeling sign-off attached to the run sheet

anti_rework_rules.rule: Identify the substrate with evidence before choosing any layer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a full strip-and-replate when the strike turns out wrong for the real metal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve skin contact and destination jurisdiction before the barrier choice
anti_rework_rules.prevents: replating a finished nickel stack that compliance later rejects

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the forming sequence before the stack column is chosen
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cracked brittle layers discovered at the sizing bench

anti_rework_rules.rule: Settle the marketing term before quoting or plating
anti_rework_rules.prevents: relabel-and-refund disputes and stacks rebuilt to earn a word

anti_rework_rules.rule: Rule on the migration mechanism before setting the gold build
anti_rework_rules.prevents: tarnish-through returns on thin gold the barrier verdict would have caught

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass the strike adhesion coupon before building underplate or gold
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending gold onto a stack already doomed to peel

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the verification plan before the first tank, not after the last
anti_rework_rules.prevents: unmeasurable stacks that can neither pass nor fail honestly

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the topcoat before final finishing and first dry handling
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recontamination and re-cleaning cycles between gold and seal

iteration_protocol.trigger: adhesion failure at verification or in the field
iteration_protocol.action: re-run substrate identification and the strike map for that job class before touching anything else

iteration_protocol.trigger: tarnish or color-shift returns inside the disclosed wear window
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the migration verdict, barrier class, and gold build class for that stack template

iteration_protocol.trigger: a regulation change or a new destination market enters the order flow
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the compliance gate and the term gate across every affected catalog stack

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier TDS revision or a new commercial system is adopted
iteration_protocol.action: update the stack catalog and every run-sheet template that cites the changed product

iteration_protocol.trigger: porosity failures cluster on a wear class
iteration_protocol.action: raise underplate quality or build, or add a sealing class, and re-verify the class

iteration_protocol.trigger: cracking reported at bends or after sizing
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank the ductility table against coupons and re-sequence forming in the affected templates

iteration_protocol.trigger: returned run logs diverge from what the stack templates predicted
iteration_protocol.action: recalibrate the templates and the intake questions from the logged outcomes

priority_rationale: The frame nodes (brief, substrate, wear class, TDS governance) come first because every layer decision cites them; the mechanism nodes precede layer choices because strikes, barriers, and topcoats exist to defeat named mechanisms; layer selection runs strike-to-topcoat in deposition order with the compliance and terms gates embedded where nickel and naming enter; and verification and the run-sheet handoff come last because they compose the architecture into an evidence-backed, executable artifact for the electrical and fixturing KBs.
